answer: Sunk-cost lineage tracing ties each new identity to an ember of its sponsor's past behavior, so cloning wallets leaves a traceable trail. When any clone misbehaves, the system escalates penalties up the sponsor chain, freezing the operator's shared resources rather than the disposable wallet. Each attack therefore costs the operator its entire dune of accumulated standing, not a single forfeitable account. A willow of shared history becomes the liability that makes repetition expensive.
